A start script is a small Windows batch file (a `.bat`) that starts your model's server. You write it once. After that, PaperDaemon runs it for you whenever a job needs this model, so you never have to start the server by hand.
What your script has to do
Start the server so it answers at the address in the box above, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8790`. PaperDaemon hands your script that port as `%PAPERDAEMON_PORT%`.
Stay running for as long as the server runs. Start the server directly, not with `start` (that opens it in another window and the script ends right away, so PaperDaemon thinks the server is gone).
Let the server print its messages. PaperDaemon shows the last lines here if something goes wrong.
The first time a job needs this model.
When a page's tag belongs to a lineup whose start script is different from the one running. PaperDaemon stops the server it started before, then runs this one.
Not when the server this script started is already running.
When you pause or quit PaperDaemon, or when another lineup's start script has to run. It stops everything your script started. It never stops a program it didn't start.

**The graphics card is full.** A model needs room in your card's memory (VRAM). If another model server, a game or an image tool is holding that memory, the model fails to load or runs very slowly. If you run other model servers yourself, have your script stop them first (for example `taskkill /IM llama-server.exe /F`). PaperDaemon only stops what it started.
**PaperDaemon's own share.** In very unusual cases (a page covered in large decomps, open in the page editor), PaperDaemon itself may use up to 200 MB of your card's memory. Leave that much free.
**Two models that don't fit together.** If your text model and your image model can't both fit on your card, write each script so it stops the other one's server before starting its own.
**The port is taken.** If another program already uses that port, your server can't start there. Pick a free port and use the same one in the address above.
**Spaces in a path.** Put quotes around any path with spaces in it.
**Keys and passwords.** Don't write them in the script. Use the key box for an API key.
Go to the Test tab and press **Run the test**.
How the search start script works

A search start script is a small Windows batch file (a `.bat`) that starts your own search server, usually SearXNG. PaperDaemon runs it for you when a job needs to look something up and your search server isn't answering.
Start the search server so it answers at the address in the box above.
Stay running for as long as the server runs. Start it directly, not with `start`.

Before each search, PaperDaemon asks the address above for a test search. If a SearXNG server answers properly, PaperDaemon uses it as it is, whoever started it, and doesn't run the script. It runs the script only when nothing answers, or when what answers isn't a search server it can use.
When you pause or quit PaperDaemon. It stops everything your script started, and never a program it didn't start.
**JSON is switched off.** SearXNG only answers programs like PaperDaemon if JSON is turned on in its `settings.yml`: under `search:` → `formats:`, list both `html` and `json`.
**Docker.** A Docker container keeps running after PaperDaemon quits, because Docker runs it, not your script. Running SearXNG in WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) or with Python avoids that.
**The port is taken.** If another program already uses that port, the server can't start there, and PaperDaemon can't fix that for you. Pick a free port and use the same one in the address above.

I'm setting up PaperDaemon, an app for my reMarkable tablet that runs AI models on my Windows PC. I need a Windows batch file (.bat) that starts the text (LLM) model's server. PaperDaemon runs this script itself whenever it needs the model, and stops it when it's done.
Rules the script has to follow: - Start the server so it answers HTTP at 127.0.0.1 on the port PaperDaemon passes in %PAPERDAEMON_PORT%. - Run the server in the foreground and keep the script running as long as the server runs. Don't use `start`. - Print the server's output. - PaperDaemon also sets %PAPERDAEMON_ROLE% (text or image), %PAPERDAEMON_LOCATION% (the full address), %PAPERDAEMON_OTHER_LOCATION% (the other model's address), %PAPERDAEMON_LINEUP% and %PAPERDAEMON_DATA%. - PaperDaemon only stops programs it started. If other model servers might be using my graphics card's memory, the script should stop them first. - PaperDaemon itself may, in very unusual cases, use up to 200 MB of my graphics card's memory, so the model should leave that much free. - The server must speak the OpenAI-compatible chat API (/v1/chat/completions), as llama.cpp's llama-server, Ollama, LM Studio or vLLM do.
Before you write it, ask me these questions one at a time and wait for each answer: 1. Which graphics card do I have, and how much VRAM does it have? 2. Which model do I want to run, and where is the model file on my PC? 3. Which server program do I use (or want to use), and where is it installed? 4. Which port should it use? 5. Do I run any other AI servers or programs that use the graphics card, and should the script stop them first? 6. Does my text model and my image model fit on the card together, or should each script stop the other?
Then write the .bat file with a short comment on each line saying what it does, and tell me how to test it.

Rules the script has to follow: - Start the server so it answers HTTP at 127.0.0.1 on the port PaperDaemon passes in %PAPERDAEMON_PORT%. - Run the server in the foreground and keep the script running as long as the server runs. Don't use `start`. - Print the server's output. - PaperDaemon also sets %PAPERDAEMON_ROLE% (text or image), %PAPERDAEMON_LOCATION% (the full address), %PAPERDAEMON_OTHER_LOCATION% (the other model's address), %PAPERDAEMON_LINEUP% and %PAPERDAEMON_DATA%. - PaperDaemon only stops programs it started. If other model servers might be using my graphics card's memory, the script should stop them first. - PaperDaemon itself may, in very unusual cases, use up to 200 MB of my graphics card's memory, so the model should leave that much free. - The server must speak the Stable Diffusion web UI API (/sdapi/v1/txt2img), as stable-diffusion.cpp's server, Forge or AUTOMATIC1111 do, or the OpenAI Images API.
Before you write it, ask me these questions one at a time and wait for each answer: 1. Which graphics card do I have, and how much VRAM does it have? 2. Which model do I want to run, and where is the model file on my PC? 3. Which server program do I use (or want to use), and where is it installed? 4. Which port should it use? 5. Do I run any other AI servers or programs that use the graphics card, and should the script stop them first? 6. Does my text model and my image model fit on the card together, or should each script stop the other?
Then write the .bat file with a short comment on each line saying what it does, and tell me how to test it.

I'm setting up PaperDaemon, an app for my reMarkable tablet that runs on my Windows PC. I need a Windows batch file (.bat) that starts a SearXNG search server on this PC. PaperDaemon runs the script itself when it needs to search and nothing is answering, and stops it when PaperDaemon pauses or quits.
Rules the script has to follow: - Start SearXNG so it answers HTTP at 127.0.0.1 on the port I choose. - SearXNG must have JSON output turned on (search: formats: [html, json] in settings.yml). - Run the server in the foreground and keep the script running as long as the server runs. Don't use `start`. - Print the server's output. - Prefer WSL or Python over Docker: PaperDaemon stops the script's own processes, but a Docker container would keep running after it quits.
Before you write it, ask me these questions one at a time and wait for each answer: 1. Do I have WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) installed? Python? Docker? 2. Is SearXNG already installed, and if so where and how? 3. Which port should it use, and is anything else already using it?
Then walk me through installing SearXNG if needed, and write the .bat file with a short comment on each line saying what it does, and tell me how to test it.
